title: Commercial and Industrial Designers
description: Design and develop manufactured products, such as cars, home appliances, and children's toys. Combine artistic talent with research on product use, marketing, and materials to create the most functional and appealing product design.

tasks.text: Prepare sketches of ideas, detailed drawings, illustrations, artwork, or blueprints, using drafting instruments, paints and brushes, or computer-aided design equipment.
Modify and refine designs, using working models, to conform with customer specifications, production limitations, or changes in design trends.
Develop industrial standards and regulatory guidelines.
Coordinate the look and function of product lines.
Design graphic material for use as ornamentation, illustration, or advertising on manufactured materials and packaging or containers.
Advise corporations on issues involving corporate image projects or problems.
Direct and coordinate the fabrication of models or samples and the drafting of working drawings and specification sheets from sketches.
Supervise assistants' work throughout the design process.
Investigate product characteristics such as the product's safety and handling qualities, its market appeal, how efficiently it can be produced, and ways of distributing, using, and maintaining it.
Participate in new product planning or market research, including studying the potential need for new products.
Develop manufacturing procedures and monitor the manufacture of their designs in a factory to improve operations and product quality.
Read publications, attend showings, and study competing products and design styles and motifs to obtain perspective and generate design concepts.

clusters.label: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People

tasks.text: Evaluate feasibility of design ideas, based on factors such as appearance, safety, function, serviceability, budget, production costs/methods, and market characteristics.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Confer with engineering, marketing, production, or sales departments, or with customers, to establish and evaluate design concepts for manufactured products.

clusters.label: Interpreting the Meaning of Information for Others

tasks.text: Present designs and reports to customers or design committees for approval and discuss need for modification.
Research production specifications, costs, production materials, and manufacturing methods and provide cost estimates and itemized production requirements.
Fabricate models or samples in paper, wood, glass, fabric, plastic, metal, or other materials, using hand or power tools.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Technology Design
skills.def: Generating or adapting equipment and technology to serve user needs.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Creative Cloud software, Adobe FreeHand MX, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Ashlar-Vellum Cobalt, Autodesk AliasStudio, Autodesk AutoCAD, Autodesk Maya.

skills.name: Graphical user interface development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which interact with users through a graphical interface. Examples: Figma.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.
